chunks: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the All-High, the Supreme.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's ownership of the heavens and the earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores God's absolute sovereignty (Mulk) and transcendence (Tanzih), affirming that He is distinct from His creation yet omnipresent. The attributes Al-'Ali and Al-'Azim are often linked to the concept of divine unity (Tawhid), reminding believers that all authority and majesty belong solely to Allah, free from any partner or equal.
